full_judgment:
Mr. Muhammad Ansar Ali, J:- This Rule arises out of an application by defendant-petitioner under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.5.86 passed by the learned District Judge, Jamalpur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 121 of 1985 confirming the judgment and order dated 28.11.85 passed by the learned Munsif, First Court, Jamalpur rejecting an application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Misc. Case No. 37 of 1985 for setting aside an ex parte decree dated 3.6.85 passed by the learned Munsif in Other Class Suit No. 32 of 1984. 

 The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid Other Class Suit No. 32 of 1984 in the First Court Munsif, Jamalpur on 4.3.84 against one Priyabala Debi predecessor of the defendant-petitioner and 3 others for permanent injunction in respect of .13 acre of land of C. S. Plot No. 53 Mouza Kursha Kongarpara within Sadar P. S. and District Jamalpur and also there was a prayer for temporary injunction. The case of the plaintiff-opposite parties was that the predecessor of the present petitioner, Priyabala Debi was a stranger to the suit-land and she had purchase .08 acre of land with a C. I. sheet but from the co-sharer of the plaintiffs and thereafter filed a partition suit being Partition Suit No. 148 of 1970 in the Court of 1st Munsif, Jamalpur and she being a stranger was not entitled to any joint possession in the suit land with the plaintiffs but still she tried to go into the possession of the suit land forcibly. Hence the suit for permanent injunction. 

 3. The said defendant Priyabala Debi, predecessor of the present petitioner filed a written statement to contest the suit contending inter alia that she filed a partition suit being Partition Suit No. 148 of 1970 and got a preliminary decree which was subsequently made final on 18.6.74 and she got possession of her share amicably. But subsequently the plaintiff-opposite parties forcibly dispossessed her from some portion of her share; that during the pendency of the aforesaid suit, the defendant Priyabala Debi interstate and on her death the petitioner was made a party in the suit on 10.4.85 by way of substitution. Thereafter the suit proceeded and 15.5.85 was fixed for hearing but on the date upon the prayer of the defendant, 3.6.85 was fixed for pre-emptory hearing of the suit. The defendant-petitioner on the date fell seriously ill and could not appear in court and as a result the suit was taken up for ex parte hearing and ultimately decreed ex parte by the learned Munsif. The defendant petitioner thereafter having recovered from his illness filed an application under order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the ex parte decree and for restoration of the suit to its original file and number. The application was registered as Misc. Case No. 37 of 1985. The defendant-petitioner examined 3 witnesses including himself as P.W. 1 and the doctor who made her treatment as P. W. 3 in support of his case and the plaintiff opposite-parties jointly filed a written objection to contest the Misc. Case and examined one witness i. e. the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 as O. P. W. 1. The learned Munsiff after hearing the Misc. Case and on consideration of the materials on record dismissed the Misc. Case on contest by an order dated 28.11.85 on a finding that the defendant failed to prove his alleged illness on the date of hearing of the suit on 3.6.85. The defendant-petitioner being aggrieved by the said judgment from the learned Munsif filed an appeal being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 121 of 1985 before the learned District Judge, Jamalpur. After the hearing both the sides the learned District Judge was pleased to dismiss the same on contest and affirmed the judgment and order of the learned Munsif of similar finding by his judgment and order dated 26.5.86. Thereafter the defendant-petitioner moved the instant application in this court and obtained the present Rule. It may be mentioned that in spite of due service of notice of the rule upon the plaintiff-opposite parties there is no appearance on their behalf to oppose the Rule. 

 From the above it appears that in the absence of the defendant if summons is found to have been duly served upon him, the Court may proceed ex parte. It does not say that the court must necessarily pass an ex parte decree in absence of the defendants. Rather the Court may decree or dismiss the suit ex parte according to the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record. Order 20 rule 4 sub-rule (2) speaks of contents of a judgment and the same is as follows:- 

 "Judgments of other Courts shall contain a concise statement of the case, the points for determination, the decision thereon, and the reasons for such decision." Again rule (5) of the said order goes further to state the following:- 

 5. Now, from a plain reading of the aforesaid provisions of law it appears that there are some legal requirements in passing a judgment whether ex parte or otherwise. In the instant case it appears that the lower appellate court has failed to examine the propriety of the impugned order dated 3.6.85 of the learned Munsif from the above angle and has only confined itself to the question of sufficient cause preventing the defendant-petitioner from appearing in the Court on the date fixed for hearing of the suit. Hence it is contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the learned District Judge has committed serious error of law in upholding the order of the learned Munsif and the ex parte decree and the same has cause a failure of justice. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has relied on a decision in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Israil Ali and others reported in 1981 B. S. C. R., vol.- V(AD), 222, wherein it has been laid down by their Lordships that. 

 "The trial Court again committed an error of procedure in not complying with the mandatory provisions. It has only been stated that P. W. 1 was examined. Exts. 1- 2(d), 2-2(b) and 3-3(1) marked and the plaintiffs case proved. This does not at all satisfy the legal requirements nor is it possible from reading the judgment, that the trial Court at all applied judicial mind; whether the plaintiffs witnesses and papers proved the plaintiffs case.... The findings recorded by the trial Court neither satisfied the legal requirements nor from such finding the alleged case of the plaintiffs was proved." 

 The learned Advocate has also relied on another decision in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Abdul Wadud and others reported in 25 D. L. R. (SC), 90, wherein it has been laid down as follows : 

 The plaint is no evidence for the proof of the case of the plaintiff. The absence of the defendant who asked for adjournment but refused on reasons assigned thereof cannot give occasion for the plaintiff to obtain ex parte decree without producing the relevant documents on the basis of which relief is sought for. The Court is bound to apply its mind with reference to the pleadings and satisfy itself as to what should be the proper proof for passing a decree on the basis of the averments made in the plaint." 

 5. In the instant case, the learned Munsif refused the defendants prayer for adjournment of the hearing and passed the following ex parte judgment and decree on 3.6.85 :- 

 It is contended by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that from a reading of the impugned ex parte judgment, it appears that the learned Munsif only recorded the deposition of the plaintiff as P. W. 1 and without proof of any document filed by the plaintiff and or marking the same as exhibits in support of the plaintiffs case and without complying with the provisions of Order 20 rule 4 sub-rule 2 and Rule 5 that means without applying his judicial mind to the facts and Circumstances of the case and the evidence on record, has arbitrarily passed the impugned ex parte judgment and decree and granted the relief for permanent injunction in favour of the plaintiff against the contesting defendant-petitioner. I myself have carefully read the impugned ex parte judgment and decree and I find that the learned Munsif has not uttered a single word in respect of possession of the parties in the suit-land though it is a suit for permanent injunction wherein question of possession is of vital importance and also about the documents which have been only filed in Court by the plaintiffs in support of his case but not legally proved and marked as exhibits in the suit. Thus it is clear that the minimum legal requirements in passing the ex parte judgment and decree have not been complied with and thus there has been gross violation of the mandatory provisions of law which has resulted in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice. The learned District Judge has totally failed to notice this vital defect in the impugned ex parte judgment and decree and illegally upheld the same without proper application of his judicial mind to the material aspect of the case. However in view of the above provisions of law and the decisions referred to above, I find much force in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and I am inclined to hold that the ex parte decree has been passed illegally and without compliance of the mandatory provisions of law and hence the impugned orders of the courts below suffer from serious legal infirmities which have caused a failure of justice and hence need be interfered with by this court in the interest of justice. Now, as regards the finding as to the sufficient cause by which the defendant-petitioner has been allegedly prevented from appearing in the trial court on the day fixed for hearing of the suit, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the same has not been based on proper consideration of the material on record and the learned Munsif has given undue weight to some minor discrepancies in the deposition of the witnesses instead of considering the materials and the vital parts of the evidence on record particularly with regard to the illness of the defendant petitioners on 3.6.85 and further the evidence of both the sides has not been judged by the Court below by equal standard and as a result has been a complete miscarriage of justice.
